newsitem.title: UK: Licht sees rising volatility of world sugar price.
newsitem.headline: Licht sees rising volatility of world sugar price.

text.p: World sugar prices look set to become increasingly volatile as exports become more concentrated in the hands of a few major producers, the managing director of German statistician F.O. Licht said on Friday.

Helmut Ahlfeld told a London conference that in 1995/96, the world's five leading exporters accounted for nearly 66 percent of gross exports, with Brazil, Thailand and Australia occupying an increasingly prominent position.

"This poses a risk of greater price instability," he said, adding that the dependency on the five -- the European Union, Cuba, Brazil, Thailand and Australia -- had arisen even though Cuba had lost its pre-eminent position as a world exporter.

Ahlfeld said cost pressures and further trade liberalisation would lead to more concentration, with production expected to shift to South America and Asia because GATT rules and marketing prospects prevented the EU from significantly expanding exports.
"There will be further concentration among exporters owing to cost pressures and continuing liberalisation, which could lead to less stable prices," he said.
